messages:
Priya S: heads-up, our canary batch for rollout 2026-03-15-rc7 is spiking 5xxs in us-west-2. noticing increased tail latency too. tagging oncall.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0321 — canary failures during rollout (trigger: canary-error-rate > 5% for 10m). Paging @Priya S, @Jared L, @Marta G.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/rc7 -> canary-batch-42 at 2177001200.

Jared L: confirming, I see spike in the canary group only. non-canary traffic looks normal. adding logs now. :mag:  

Ethan K: logs show a mix of 502s and 504s from grpc-proxy. stacktrace points at kv-cache eviction errors in runtime.

Marta G: I'm trying to open the canary dashboard but the canary-error-rate panel is empty. looks like the overlay is missing metrics for that shard. anyone else?

Priya S: same — dashboard panels return "no data" for that metric. that explains why SLO dashboards looked flat earlier. we might have a telemetry gap.

Noah (SRE Lead): critical question: do we have user impact or is this isolated to canaries? need to evaluate before killing flag or rolling back.

Jared L: quick smoke vs prod: hitting a few internal endpoints that are routed to canary — some customers behind that routing might see errors. not widespread but non-zero.

Ethan K: can we confirm log shipping? I ran `curl http://telemetry-push.us-west-2/health` and got 200 but the canary index shows 0 docs. suspect router tagging problem.

Marta G: FYI the oncall runbook step 3 assumes the dashboard exists — it doesn't. runbook says to check `dashboards/canary-error-rate` which is empty. adding note.

Priya S: decision time — three mitigations: 1) kill feature flag for this cohort, 2) rollback the canary, 3) keep canary and triage deeper. propose kill flag for batch-42 while we investigate. lower blast radius.

Jared L: +1 kill flag. fewer moving parts. how do we flip it?

Ethan K: flip with `ffctl toggle rollout-batch-42 --off --actor=oncall` (only available to infra team). I will run with confirmation.

Ethan K: running now...

Ethan K: ```
$ ffctl toggle rollout-batch-42 --off --actor=EthanK --reason "canary 5xx spike, missing canary metrics"
SUCCESS: rollout-batch-42 state -> OFF
```

oncall-bot: Action logged: feature flag rollout-batch-42 set to OFF by Ethan K at 2177002460.

Marta G: seeing errors drop in the canary logs immediately. proxy errors cease within ~30s. panels now start showing partial telemetry (still some lag).

Priya S: good. moving to customer impact assessment. Jared, can you run the query for affected customer IDs from the last 20m and estimate requests impacted?

Jared L: running: ```
select count(*) from requests where route in ('canary-route-1','canary-route-2') and status >= 500 and ts > now() - interval '20 minutes';
``` result -> 1,372 errors; estimate ~0.03% of total traffic, but concentrated across 4 paying customers.

Noah (SRE Lead): put customer-impact tag on incident and notify CS for the four customers. Priya, please escalate with RPMs.

Priya S: pinging CS_channel and RPMs now: "Heads up — partial errors for customers A,B,C,D during recent canary. We killed the flag, errors stopped, we'll follow up with postmortem." :email: 

Ethan K: note — the initial root cause appears to be a telemetry/metric-shipping mismatch combined with a runtime cache eviction bug exposed by new kernel change in rc7. telemetry gap made the dashboards blind; that delayed detection by product owners.

Marta G: action items I captured: 1) postmortem to include missing dashboard discovery, 2) add health-check for canary metric pipeline, 3) revert kernel change or rerun with fix in a controlled environment, 4) add explicit alert when canary dashboards return "no data".

Priya S: assigning tasks: Marta will own dashboard/alert work, Ethan will follow-up on ff rollback and kernel revert, Jared will run customer impact analysis and follow up with CS, Noah will coordinate postmortem and severity classification.

Noah (SRE Lead): marking incident as RESOLVED for now — mitigation succeeded (flag OFF), limited customer impact, no further pager activity. we'll keep the incident open in the tracker until postmortem is posted.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0321 status -> RESOLVED by Noah at 2177004078.

Priya S: quick note for follow-up meeting: we need a test that simulates metric backfills so dashboards don't return silent zeros; that's what tripped us.

Jared L: logging commands and queries used into the incident doc. will add a snippet of the ffctl command and the SQL.

Marta G: added temporary dashboard fallback to surface raw proxy 5xx count until metric pipeline is fixed.

Priya S: thanks team. postmortem owner: Noah. ETA for draft: EOD +2. closing the thread here, will cross-post postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
